parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a SQL statement to list the name and salary of each employee in the Sales department who earns more than $13,000.  (2 marks)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Write a SQL statement that returns the number of employees in each department whose average salary is 18000 or more. (2 marks)
[--Answer:
(a) SELECT NAME, AMOUNT
FROM EMPLOYEE E INNER JOIN SALARY S ON E.POINT = S.POINT
WHERE DEPT = 'SALES' AND AMOUNT > 13000
(b) SELECT DEPT, COUNT(*)
FROM EMPLOYEE E LEFT JOIN SALARY S ON E.POINT = S.POINT
GROUP BY DEPT
HAVING AVG(AMOUNT) >= 18000
--]

parts.label: a
parts.text: List the car types that are available in the Kwun Tong district but not Yuen Long district using MINUS.  (2 marks)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The company creates another table RENTAL to store information on the car rental, and below are some records of RENTAL.
RENTAL
CID
CUS

END
Y101

The company wants to keep track of how many cars they have available for rent at each location and the total number of cars they have at all locations. They plan to notify their customers if the number of available cars at a specific location exceeds 5. If the END column in RENTAL is null, it means that the rental period has not yet ended and the car is not available for rent. The value of END will be set only after the rental period has ended.
Write a SQL command to list the location and number of cars available.  (3 marks)
[--Answer:
(a) SELECT TYPE FROM CARS WHERE LOCATION = 'Kwun Tong'
MINUS
SELECT TYPE FROM CARS WHERE LOCATION = 'Yuen Long'
(b) SELECT C.LOCATION, COUNT(*) AS NUM_CARS_AVAILABLE
FROM CARS C LEFT JOIN RENTAL R ON C.CID = R.CID
WHERE R.CID IS NULL OR R.END IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY C.LOCATION
HAVING COUNT(*) <= 5
--]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write an SQL statement to retrieve the identity code of all members who have volunteered for the voluntary work named "Food Bank".  (2 marks)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
List the name of members who do not join any service.  (3 marks)
[--Answer:
(a) SELECT R.MID
FROM VOLUNTARY_WORKS V INNER JOIN RECORD R ON V.VID = R.VID
WHERE VNAME = 'Food Bank'
Alternatives:
SELECT R.MID
FROM RECORD R
WHERE R.VID IN (
SELECT V.VID
FROM VOLUNTARY_WORKS V
WHERE VNAME = 'Food Bank'
)
(b) SELECT MNAME
FROM MEMBER M LEFT JOIN RECORD R ON M.MID = R.MID
WHERE R.MID IS NULL
Alternatives:
SELECT MNAME
FROM MEMBER M
WHERE M.MID NOT IN (
SELECT R.MID
FROM RECORD R
)
--]

parts.label: a
parts.text: List the names of all teams that have played all the games in the tournament. (3 marks)

(4 marks)

FROM TEAM T, TEMP P
WHERE T.TID = P.TID AND P.AVG_SCORE = (
SELECT MAX(AVG_SCORE)
FROM TEMP
)
--]

Honey theatre company uses a database with two tables PLAY and STAFF to store information on plays and staff. Staff members can access the database to acquire information.

PLAY

Description

Example

Write SQL commands to complete the following tasks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: List the name of the play that has a staff member with "Chan" in their name.  (2 marks)

parts.label: i
parts.text: Create a view named JOINALL that displays the staff ID of the staff members who have assisted in all the plays. Alias the number of plays as NOOFPLAY.  (3 marks)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: Use the view created in (b)(i) to display the staff name in the ACTOR department.  (3 marks)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Select all the staff members who have not performed in any play that was written by 'William Shakespeare'.  (3 marks)
[--Answer:
(a) SELECT PNAME
FROM PLAY P, STAFF S, PERFORMANCE E
WHERE P.PID = E.PID AND S.SID = E.SID
WHERE SNAME LIKE '%Chan%'

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(i)  CREATE VIEW JOINALL AS
SELECT SID, COUNT(DISTINCT.PID) AS NOOFPLAY
FROM PERFORMANCE
GROUP BY SID
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT.PID) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM PLAY)
(ii) SELECT SNAME
FROM STAFF
WHERE DEPT = 'Actor' AND SID IN (
SELECT SID
FROM JOINALL
)
(c) SELECT *
FROM STAFF
WHERE SID NOT IN (
SELECT SID
FROM PERFORMANCE P, PLAY Y
WHERE P.PID = Y.PID
WHERE WRITER = 'William Shakespeare'
)
--]

items.stem:
A company manages a job application system that allows interns to apply for multiple jobs. Each job has a unique job ID and is assigned to only one department. Interns can apply for multiple jobs, but each application is for only one job, and they can only apply for jobs in the same department as themselves. The company uses a database with multiple tables to store the information.
Here are the table structures.
DEPARTMENT
Field name
Description
DID
Identity code of the department
DNAME
Name of the department
JOB
Field name
Description
JID
Identity code of the job
JTITLE
Title of the job
DID
Identity code of the department
INTERNS
Field name
Description
IID
Identity code of the intern
NAME
Name of the intern
EMAIL
Email of the intern
DID
Identity code of the department the intern belongs to
APPLICATION
Field name
Description
AID
Identity code of the application
IID
Identity code of the intern
JID
Identity code of the job
ADATE
Application date and time

parts.label: i
parts.text: Write a SQL command to create a NOJ index file with the primary key of JOB.  (2 marks)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: What is the purpose of creating an index?  (1 mark)

parts.label: b
parts.text: The manager needs to contact the interns who have not applied for any jobs during the month of June. Write a SQL statement to retrieve these interns’ names and email addresses.  (3 marks)

parts.label: c
parts.text: The manager would like to see the number of job applications made by each intern in the FINANCE department if they have applied for at least one job. Write a SQL command to display the name of interns and the number of jobs applied.  (3 marks)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
List the names of interns who have applied for a job that is not in their own department. (3 marks)
[--Answer:

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(i) CREATE INDEX NOJ ON JOB(JID)
(ii) It improves the speed of searching.
(b) SELECT NAME, EMAIL
FROM INTERNS
WHERE IID NOT IN (
SELECT IID
FROM APPLICATION
WHERE MONTH(ADATE) = 6
)
(c) SELECT I.NAME, COUNT(*) AS NUM_APPLICATIONS
FROM INTERNS I, APPLICATION A, DEPARTMENT D
WHERE I.IID = A.IID AND I.DID = D.DID AND DNAME = 'FINANCE'
GROUP BY A.IID
(d) SELECT I.NAME
FROM INTERNS I, APPLICATION A, JOB J
WHERE I.IID = A.IID AND A.JID = J.JID AND I.DID <> J.DID
--]

items.stem:
The Sports Union is organising a basketball tournament. The person in charge, Mr Mak maintains a database table named GAME and TEAM to store information on various games and teams in the tournament.
TEAM
Field name
Description
TID
Identity code of the home team
TNAME
Name of the team
Primary key: TID
GAME
Field name
Description
GID
Identity code of the game
HTID
Identity code of the home team
HTS
Score of the home team
ATID
Identity code of the away team
ATS
Score of the away team
GD
Date of the game
VENUE
Location of the game
Primary key: GID
Foreign key: HTID. ATID

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Write a SQL statement to list the teams’ names that have not won any games in the tournament.
(4 marks)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
What is the purpose of the following SQL commands?  (2 marks)
CREATE VIEW team_scores AS
SELECT HTS AS score
FROM GAME
UNION ALL
SELECT ATS AS score
FROM GAME;
SELECT AVG(score)
FROM team_scores;

parts.label: i
parts.text: Create a view named HOME_TEAM_SCORE to display the total score gained by each team when they are in the home team.  (2 marks)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: Create a view named AWAY_TEAM_SCORE to display the total score gained by each team when they are an away team.  (2 marks)

parts.label: iii
parts.text:
Based on the two views created, list the final score of each team gained, and order them in descending order. (4 marks)
[--Answer:
(a) SELECT TNAME
FROM TEAM
WHERE TID NOT IN (SELECT HTID
FROM GAME
WHERE HTS > ATS
UNION ALL
SELECT ATID
FROM GAME
WHERE ATS > HTS)
(b) Find out the average score of all teams across all their games.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(i)  CREATE VIEW HOME_TEAM_SCORE AS
SELECT HTID AS TID, SUM(HTS) AS THS
FROM GAME
GROUP BY HTID
(ii) CREATE VIEW AWAY_TEAM_SCORE AS
SELECT ATID AS TID, SUM(ATS) AS TAS
FROM GAME
GROUP BY ATID
(iii) SELECT H.TID, SUM(THS + TAS) AS score
FROM HOME_TEAM_SCORE H, AWAY_TEAM_SCORE A
WHERE H.TID = A.TID
GROUP BY H.TID
ORDER BY score DESC  Alternatives:  SELECT A.TID, SUM(THS + TAS) AS score
FROM HOME_TEAM_SCORE H, AWAY_TEAM_SCORE A
WHERE H.TID = A.TID
GROUP BY A.TID
ORDER BY score DESC
--]
